cards.prompt: Define Software test-model state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A predicate-defined region of state-variable valuations treated as behaviorally equivalent for the specified transition conditions, expected actions, invariants, and test-selection objectives.
required_concepts: A test-model state is a predicate-defined region of state-variable valuations.
Valuations in that region are treated as behaviorally equivalent for specified transition conditions and expected actions.
The equivalence also respects specified invariants and test-selection objectives.
major_error_concepts: Naming a state with prose that cannot classify concrete prestates consistently.

cards.prompt: Define Test-model transition effect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified next-state relation, output, exception, event, or external effect required when a trigger and guard are evaluated from an eligible prestate.
required_concepts: The specified next-state relation, output, exception, event, or external effect required when a trigger and guard are evaluated from an eligible prestate.
major_error_concepts: Recording only the destination-state label while ignoring outputs or effects required by the same transition.

cards.prompt: Define Software test-model transition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified relation binding source-state predicate, trigger, guard classification, required effect, destination-state predicate, and expected observations for one modeled behavior step.
required_concepts: A test-model transition is a specified relation for one modeled behavior step.
A test-model transition binds a source-state predicate, trigger, and guard classification.
A test-model transition binds the required effect, destination-state predicate, and expected observations.
major_error_concepts: Describing transitions only as arrows between labels without executable predicates or observable effects.

cards.prompt: Define Test-model transition trigger. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified call, command, event, timeout, input, or environmental occurrence whose attempted application may produce a modeled state transition or specified rejection.
required_concepts: A test-model trigger is a specified call, command, event, timeout, input, or environmental occurrence.
Attempting the trigger may produce a modeled state transition or a specified rejection.
major_error_concepts: Treating internal helper calls as model triggers when they are not independently observable or controllable behaviors.

cards.prompt: Define software test object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A software test object is the exact function, class, component, service boundary, executable, configuration, migration, or system whose behavior a test directly exercises or observes.
required_concepts: A software test object is the exact software subject whose behavior a test directly exercises or observes.
The subject may be a function, class, component, service boundary, executable, configuration, migration, or system.
major_error_concepts: Naming a wrapper or dependency as the test object when the asserted behavior belongs to a different subject.

cards.prompt: Define Executable-test observation phase. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The deliberate capture of returned values, state, events, calls, files, diagnostics, exceptions, and external effects needed by the specified oracle after or during the action.
required_concepts: The observation phase deliberately captures returned values, state, events, calls, files, diagnostics, exceptions, or external effects.
An executable-test observation phase captures observations needed by the specified oracle.
The capture may occur during or after the test action.
major_error_concepts: Observing only a convenient return value while the requirement concerns unrecorded persistent or external state.

cards.prompt: Define Software-test order sensitivity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A failure or verdict change conditioned on which tests, fixtures, or cleanup operations execute earlier, usually through undeclared shared state, resource consumption, or global configuration.
required_concepts: Test order sensitivity means that a failure or verdict changes according to which tests, fixtures, or cleanup operations execute earlier.
The change usually propagates through undeclared shared state, resource consumption, or global configuration.
major_error_concepts: Fixing the test order instead of identifying and controlling the shared dependency.

cards.prompt: Define Executable-test outcome taxonomy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified mutually distinguishable classifications for passed, failed, errored, skipped, expected-failed, unexpectedly-passed, deselected, timed-out, interrupted, and uncollected test instances.
required_concepts: A test outcome taxonomy defines specified mutually distinguishable classifications for executable test instances.
The outcome classes include passed, failed, errored, skipped, expected-failed, unexpectedly-passed, deselected, timed-out, interrupted, and uncollected.
major_error_concepts: Collapsing every nonpass into failed or treating expected failures as evidence that the underlying behavior passed.

cards.prompt: Define Software-test rerun policy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified rule governing which outcomes may be retried, how many times, under what environment, how attempts are reported, and how final gate status preserves initial failures.
required_concepts: A test rerun policy is a specified rule for which outcomes may be retried and how many retries are allowed.
A software-test rerun policy specifies the retry environment and how every attempt is reported.
A software-test rerun policy's final gate status preserves the initial failures.
major_error_concepts: Reporting only the last successful retry and hiding instability from evidence consumers.

cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Executable-test scope impose?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** The declared software boundary, real and replaced collaborators, process and resource boundary, environment, and observation surface exercised by one test or test population.

**Worked check.** Record that a repository test uses a real database adapter but replaces the remote transport at an injected seam.
required_concepts: Executable-test scope is the declared software boundary with declared real or replaced collaborators.
Executable-test scope declares the process and resource boundary and the environment.
Executable-test scope declares the observation surface exercised by one test or test population.
major_error_concepts: Inferring scope from a filename such as unit or integration instead of inspecting actual dependency execution.

cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Software test seam impose?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** A reviewed location where a dependency, input, effect, clock, resource, or observation can be replaced or controlled without silently changing the behavior named by the test claim.

**Worked check.** Inject a transport interface at construction while leaving serialization and retry policy inside the real component.
required_concepts: A test seam is a reviewed location where a dependency, input, effect, clock, resource, or observation can be replaced or controlled.
Using the seam must not silently change the behavior named by the test claim.
major_error_concepts: Adding a seam that bypasses the production path whose behavior the test purports to exercise.

cards.prompt: Define Executable-test setup phase. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified harness operations that establish required prestate, resources, dependency configuration, and observation hooks before the primary test action begins.
required_concepts: The setup phase consists of specified harness operations performed before the primary test action begins.
Setup-phase operations establish required prestate, resources, and dependency configuration.
Setup-phase operations establish the observation hooks needed by the test.
major_error_concepts: Hiding assertions or product actions inside setup so failures cannot be attributed to the intended phase.

cards.prompt: Define Executable-test teardown phase. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An executable-test teardown phase runs registered release, restoration, final-observation, and cleanup operations on controlled runner exits after success, failure, skip, or error; process kill, interpreter crash, machine loss, or setup failure before registration requires external isolation or cleanup recovery.
required_concepts: On controlled runner exits, teardown runs registered release, restoration, final-observation, and cleanup operations.
Controlled exits include success, failure, skip, and error after teardown has been registered.
Process kill, interpreter crash, or machine loss can prevent registered teardown from running.
Setup failure before registration or an uncontrolled exit requires external isolation or cleanup recovery.
major_error_concepts: Running cleanup only on the passing path and allowing failed cases to contaminate later executions.

cards.prompt: Define Software-test verdict. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The result of applying one identified oracle procedure and applicability rule to specified expected and observed results, including pass, fail, unjudged, invalid, or inconclusive classification.
required_concepts: A test verdict results from applying one identified oracle procedure and its applicability rule.
The oracle is applied to specified expected and observed results.
The verdict classifies the case as pass, fail, unjudged, invalid, or inconclusive.
major_error_concepts: Calling every nonexceptional execution a pass or every tool error a product failure.

cards.prompt: With all integers as the input domain and exactly the nonnegative integers accepted, what three-value boundary-analysis cases surround the selected boundary value 0, and what are their expected outcomes?
cards.definition: For the selected boundary value 0, use its predecessor -1, the value 0, and its successor 1. Here -1 is rejected, while 0 and 1 are accepted because the acceptance rule is n >= 0. This describes the neighborhood of the selected boundary value, not a claim that every boundary value identified elsewhere in a complete partition model has been covered. In domains without a representable neighbor, record the absence rather than inventing a value.
required_concepts: Select -1, 0 and 1 around the chosen integer boundary value 0.
Reject -1 and accept 0 and 1 under the stated nonnegative-integer rule.
major_error_concepts: Selecting only the boundary value.
Claiming the successor of any inclusive lower bound must be valid without considering the actual accepted domain.

cards.prompt: Define Software-test timing sensitivity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A failure or verdict change conditioned on deadlines, sleeps, polling, clock resolution, scheduler delays, timezones, wall versus monotonic time, or event ordering under recorded timing circumstances.
required_concepts: Timing sensitivity means that a software-test failure or verdict changes because of a timing condition.
The condition may involve deadlines, sleeps, polling, clock resolution, scheduler delay, timezones, wall-versus-monotonic time, or event order.
The relevant timing circumstances are recorded.
major_error_concepts: Increasing timeouts until a test passes and calling the underlying synchronization defect fixed.

cards.prompt: Define Numerical tolerance contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified acceptance rule defining absolute, relative, combined, or domain-specific error bounds, reference scale, exceptional values, and comparison population for numerical results.
required_concepts: A numerical tolerance contract is a specified acceptance rule for numerical results.
A numerical tolerance contract defines absolute, relative, combined, or domain-specific error bounds.
A numerical tolerance contract defines reference scale, exceptional-value handling, and the comparison population.
major_error_concepts: Choosing a tolerance after observing the implementation error solely to make the current case pass.

cards.prompt: Define Verification-tool assumption. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An accepted condition about analyzer, runner, instrumentation, solver, model checker, compiler, library, or report correctness and configuration needed to interpret generated evidence.
required_concepts: A verification-tool assumption is a condition about a tool's correctness or configuration that the evidence accepts rather than establishes.
The tool may be an analyzer, runner, instrument, solver, model checker, compiler, library, or report system.
The accepted condition is needed to interpret the tool-generated evidence.
major_error_concepts: Treating tool output as infallible while version, configuration, known limitations, or execution errors remain unreviewed.

cards.prompt: A model has three eligible valid transitions t1, t2 and t3. Tests are known to execute t1 and t2 but not t3, without asserting their outputs/effects. What is valid-transition coverage, and what does it not establish?
cards.definition: Valid-transition coverage counts distinct eligible valid transitions exercised over the eligible total: here 2/3. It records exercised behavior paths, not successful oracle verification of all their effects. Report outcome assertions separately; visiting all states alone also need not exercise every transition.
required_concepts: Compute 2/3 from two distinct executed valid transitions out of three eligible ones.
Explain that this does not establish that expected outputs/effects were checked or correct.
major_error_concepts: Setting ordinary valid-transition coverage to zero solely because output assertions were absent.
Inferring all-transition execution from state visitation alone.
Claiming the coverage fraction proves correct transition effects.

cards.prompt: Define State-transition pair case. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A designed two-step sequence selected to exercise an ordered pair of adjacent transitions whose intermediate state can expose history, update, or guard defects invisible in isolated steps.
required_concepts: A transition-pair case is a designed two-step sequence exercising an ordered pair of adjacent transitions.
A transition-pair case's intermediate state can expose history, update, or guard defects that isolated transition steps do not reveal.
major_error_concepts: Executing two unrelated transitions without verifying the intermediate state that makes their adjacency meaningful.

cards.prompt: A model has t1: A -> B and t2: B -> C, with the sole eligible adjacent pair (t1,t2). One test starts at A and executes only t1; a separate test starts at B and executes only t2. What are individual-transition and transition-pair coverage? Do either alone establish correct outputs?
cards.definition: Both individual transitions were exercised, giving 2/2 = 100% individual-transition coverage. The ordered pair was never executed consecutively within one sequence, so pair coverage is 0/1 = 0%. In general, pair coverage counts distinct eligible adjacent pairs exercised over the eligible pair total. Correct outputs/effects require separate oracle evidence.
required_concepts: Give individual-transition coverage as 2/2 or 100%.
Give transition-pair coverage as 0/1 or 0%, since no sequence executes t1 immediately followed by t2.
Separate exercising the paths from establishing correct outputs/effects.
major_error_concepts: Concatenating separate reset tests as if they exercised one adjacent pair.
Inferring pair coverage merely from coverage of every individual transition.
Treating coverage alone as proof of correct effects.

cards.prompt: Define State-transition software test case. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A designed case binding an exact modeled prestate, trigger and parameters, guard classification, expected transition or rejection, destination, outputs, effects, and model-to-software trace.
required_concepts: A transition test case binds an exact modeled prestate, trigger and parameters, and guard classification.
A transition test case specifies the expected transition or rejection, destination, outputs, and effects.
A transition test case includes a model-to-software trace.
major_error_concepts: Inferring the prestate from prior test execution instead of releasing it as part of the case.

cards.prompt: For accepted integers 0 through 3 inclusive, with every other integer rejected, choose two-value boundary-analysis cases at both acceptance cuts. Why are 0 and 1 not the lower-cut pair?
cards.definition: Two-value boundary analysis samples the nearest domain values in the adjacent partitions. Here use -1 (reject), 0 (accept), 3 (accept), and 4 (reject). The lower cut is between -1 and 0; 0 and 1 are both in the accepted partition.
required_concepts: Select -1 and 0 at the lower cut, and 3 and 4 at the upper cut.
Identify -1 and 4 as rejected and 0 and 3 as accepted.
Explain that 0 and 1 fail to straddle the lower acceptance boundary.
major_error_concepts: Calling 0 and 1 the lower acceptance-cut pair for this domain.
Rejecting boundary-plus-adjacent-partition-neighbor selection as inherently incorrect.

cards.prompt: Define Software under-specification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specification defect in which materially unintended behaviors remain permitted because required cases, relations, state constraints, effects, failures, or quality bounds are absent or too weak.
required_concepts: Under-specification is a defect in which materially unintended behaviors remain permitted by a specification.
The permission results when required cases, relations, state constraints, effects, failures, or quality bounds are absent or too weak.
major_error_concepts: Reporting successful verification against a weak clause as evidence that the intended implementation is correct.

cards.prompt: Define Unit-test scope. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An executable-test scope centered on one small test object with collaborators controlled enough to isolate its local state transitions, outputs, exceptions, and effects.
required_concepts: Unit-test scope centers an executable test on one small test object.
Collaborators are controlled enough to isolate the object's local state transitions, outputs, exceptions, and effects.
major_error_concepts: Defining unit solely as a function or as a test that never touches a filesystem or process.

cards.prompt: Define Untested software candidate population. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit eligible conditions, values, combinations, states, transitions, sequences, environments, or scopes receiving no selected or executed oracle-bearing case in the specified study.
required_concepts: An untested candidate population is the explicit set of eligible candidates receiving no selected or executed oracle-bearing case in a specified study.
Candidates may be conditions, values, combinations, states, transitions, sequences, environments, or scopes.
major_error_concepts: Defining untested space only as source lines not executed or cases not yet written.

cards.prompt: Define Valid-domain software case. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A designed case whose complete prestate and inputs satisfy the specified syntactic, semantic, relational, environmental, and authorization constraints applicable to the tested behavior.
required_concepts: A valid-domain case has a complete prestate and inputs satisfying all specified constraints applicable to the tested behavior.
Applicable constraints may be syntactic, semantic, relational, environmental, authorization based, or a combination of these.
major_error_concepts: Calling each field valid independently while their combination violates a relational or state constraint.

cards.prompt: Define Valid software equivalence partition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An equivalence partition whose members satisfy all applicable specified domain constraints and therefore share an expected accepted behavior for the named condition.
required_concepts: Every member of a valid equivalence partition satisfies all applicable specified domain constraints.
Members of the partition share an expected accepted behavior for the named condition.
major_error_concepts: Combining all syntactically valid inputs even when semantic rules assign different outcomes or effects.

cards.prompt: Define Valid software state transition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A modeled transition whose source state, trigger parameters, guard, and environment satisfy the specified enabling conditions and therefore require the specified destination and effects.
required_concepts: A valid state transition has a source state, trigger parameters, guard, and environment satisfying the specified enabling conditions.
When enabled, the transition requires the specified destination and effects.
major_error_concepts: Calling any implementation-observed state change valid without comparing it to the specified guard and effect clauses.

cards.prompt: Define Software-verification assumption. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A proposition accepted without being established by the current evidence and required for the specification, oracle, model, tool result, or implementation correspondence to support its stated claim.
required_concepts: A verification assumption is a proposition accepted without being established by the current evidence.
The proposition is required for a specification, oracle, model, tool result, or implementation correspondence to support its stated claim.
major_error_concepts: Omitting assumptions so a conditional result appears unconditional and broader than the encoded problem.

cards.prompt: Define software-verification claim. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A software-verification claim is a falsifiable statement that an identified software subject satisfies an identified specification over an explicit behavior and environment scope under declared assumptions and evidence criteria.
required_concepts: A software-verification claim is a falsifiable statement about an identified software subject and identified specification.
A software-verification claim states an explicit behavior and environment scope.
A software-verification claim states the declared assumptions and evidence criteria under which the subject satisfies the specification.
major_error_concepts: Using an evaluative adjective such as correct or safe without a bound subject, specification, scope, assumptions, and falsifier.

cards.prompt: A bounded buffer has capacity 2. Its contract says push may be called when full, but must then reject the item and keep length 2. Starting empty, three push calls produce observed lengths 1, 2, 3. Why is this a counterexample to the contract?
cards.definition: After the first two pushes the buffer is full. The third call is in the operation's specified domain because full-buffer pushes have an explicit rejection rule. Observing length 3 contradicts the required unchanged length 2 and capacity bound. One applicable violating trace refutes the universal contract; the trace need not be globally smallest.
required_concepts: Identify the third call at full capacity as explicitly covered by the contract.
Contrast its observed length 3 with required rejection and unchanged length 2.
Explain that this valid applicable trace contradicts the universal contract.
major_error_concepts: Dismissing the third call as outside the contract despite its explicit full-buffer rule.
Claiming a single applicable violation cannot refute a universal promise.
Requiring a globally smallest trace before any counterexample is valid.

cards.prompt: Define Verification method entry criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified prerequisite condition such as stable subject, clean baseline, reviewed specification, valid domain, isolated environment, reconciled prior evidence, or authorized resource bound required before one method begins.
required_concepts: A verification entry criterion is a specified prerequisite that must hold before one verification method begins.
An entry criterion may concern a stable subject, clean baseline, reviewed specification, valid domain, isolation, reconciled evidence, or authorized resources.
major_error_concepts: Launching expensive or destructive methods while their prerequisite evidence remains unstable.

cards.prompt: Define Verification method exit criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified condition for completing, pausing, or escalating one method based on population disposition, open findings, resource limits, contradiction status, reproducibility, artifacts, reviews, and residual acceptance.
required_concepts: A verification exit criterion is a specified condition for when one method is completed, paused, or escalated.
The decision may depend on population disposition, open findings, resource limits, contradictions, reproducibility, artifacts, reviews, and residual acceptance.
major_error_concepts: Ending a method when a target metric turns green while material findings remain unreconciled.

cards.prompt: Define Software verification strategy layer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified grouping of methods by feedback speed, subject scope, environment realism, search depth, evidence class, cost, and failure-localization role rather than by prestige or test label alone.
required_concepts: A verification layer is a specified grouping by feedback speed, subject scope, realism, search depth, evidence class, cost, and failure-localization role.
The grouping is not determined by method prestige or a test label alone.
major_error_concepts: Treating layers as a universal pyramid with mandated counts or percentages.

cards.prompt: What is a verification method candidate, and how must its claim-risk region, prerequisites, and limits be specified?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** A specified proposed dynamic, generative, structural, mutation, static, symbolic, solver, verifier, model-checking, or failure-isolation method considered for one claim-risk region with prerequisites and limits explicit.

**Worked check.** Consider property search, mutation analysis, and symbolic contracts separately for a parser normalization claim.
required_concepts: A verification method candidate is a specified proposed method for one claim-risk region.
The method may be dynamic, generative, structural, mutation based, static, symbolic, solver based, model checking, or failure isolating.
A verification method candidate has explicit prerequisites and limits.
major_error_concepts: Selecting a familiar tool before identifying the evidence object and claim it can produce.

cards.prompt: Define Verification strategy resource budget. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified allocation of wall time, compute, memory, storage, test environments, reviewer effort, solver limits, fuzz executions, and mutation runs across claim-risk regions and methods.
required_concepts: A verification resource budget is a specified allocation across claim-risk regions and methods.
A resource budget may allocate wall time, compute, memory, storage, environments, reviewer effort, solver limits, fuzz executions, or mutation runs.
major_error_concepts: Spending by tool popularity or arbitrary equal shares rather than evidence need and residual risk.

cards.prompt: How should a layered verification stopping rule distinguish satisfying quality exit criteria from reaching a time or resource limit? If work remains at the limit, what should the report say?
cards.definition: A plan can stop a run when its resource bound is reached even if quality criteria remain unmet. Record the reason, completed evidence, unresolved findings and unexamined work; do not relabel them as passed. Claiming quality completion or accepting release risk requires the separately specified criteria and authorized decisions, not merely spent time or a green subset of checks.
required_concepts: A declared resource limit can legitimately end the current run without satisfying quality criteria.
Retain the actual completed evidence and unresolved/unexamined work in the stop report.
Do not infer quality completion or release approval solely from the resource stop.
major_error_concepts: Treating budget exhaustion as proof that all required verification passed.
Claiming an agent must continue past a declared resource stop merely because some quality work remains.
Silently dropping unresolved work or unexamined cases at the stopping point.

cards.prompt: Define layered software-verification strategy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A layered software-verification strategy maps claims and risks to complementary static, dynamic, formal, and review methods, including evidence dependencies, execution order, stopping rules, contradictions, assumptions, and residual risk.
required_concepts: A layered verification strategy maps claims and risks to complementary static, dynamic, formal, and review methods.
A layered verification strategy specifies evidence dependencies, execution order, and stopping rules.
A layered verification strategy records contradictions, assumptions, and residual risk.
major_error_concepts: Calling a list of tools a verification strategy without mapping methods to claims, risks, evidence, and residual uncertainty.

cards.prompt: Define Software-verification witness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A concrete input, state, model, execution, or derivation satisfying an existential verification condition under recorded assumptions without establishing a universal claim beyond that condition.
required_concepts: A verification witness is a concrete input, state, model, execution, or derivation satisfying an existential condition.
The witness satisfies that condition under recorded assumptions.
A software-verification witness does not establish a universal claim beyond the existential condition.
major_error_concepts: Generalizing one satisfying witness into proof that all inputs or executions satisfy the specification.

description: A definition-recall course deck covering core concepts in Software Testing I.
